services.title: Five services, one app, one care team
services.body: Residents choose what they need. Your association, facility team or family sees everything that matters from one place.

items.name: Doctor consultations
items.desc: Residents describe how they feel and book the right specialist, from cardiology to dermatology, usually the same evening. Their health record is shared with the doctor only if they choose.

items.name: Medicine delivery
items.desc: Orders go to partner pharmacies nearby and arrive at the door. Every order is checked against the resident's allergy list before it is sent.
points: Order from an e-prescription or a photo

items.name: Lab tests at home
items.short: Sample collection, reports in the app
items.desc: A trained phlebotomist collects samples at home in a slot that suits the resident. Reports arrive in the app with values outside range clearly flagged.
points: Share a report with a doctor in one tap

items.name: Visit companion
items.short: Escort to the hospital and back
items.desc: For residents who shouldn't go alone, a verified, elder-care trained companion picks them up, stays through the visit and brings them home, with live updates for family.

items.name: Emergency SOS
items.short: Nearest ambulance, records to the ER
items.desc: One tap alerts the nearest ambulance and the community desk together. The crew gives first aid at the door and takes the resident to a network hospital that already has their history.
points: Alerts ambulance and desk at once
Medical history sent to the ER

sos.title: When every minute counts, nobody has to make a phone call.
sos.body: One tap alerts the nearest ambulance and your community desk together. Security opens the gate, the crew gives first aid at the door, and the patient's medical history reaches the hospital before they do.

steps.sub: Community desk alerted at the same time
No time lost at the entrance

items.b: Built around your gates, towers and association, or around one family's home. Residents are verified by home.
Ambulances on standby nearby, with security alerted the moment SOS is pressed.
Vitals, conditions, allergies and medicines in one place, so every doctor and ER sees the same picture.
Each resident chooses what doctors and hospitals can see. Associations and employers never see medical details.
Enrolled neighbourhood pharmacies, labs and network hospitals, so help is close and familiar.
Doctors and companions who speak Telugu, Hindi, English and more, matched to each resident.

gated.b: We meet your committee, map the gates and agree the services you want.
Security and the community desk are trained on SOS alerts and ambulance access.
A health camp at the clubhouse records vitals and sets up each villa on the app.
Services switch on for every home. Your console shows activity from day one.

apartment.b: We meet the RWA or facility team and agree the services for each tower.
Security, lift operators and the help desk are trained on SOS and stretcher access.
Health desks in each tower lobby record vitals and set up every flat on the app.
Services switch on tower by tower. Your console tracks requests by block.

family.t: A call with our care team
family.b: We understand who needs care, where they live and which services help most.
Add parents or relatives; adult children can manage their care from their own phone.
A visit records vitals, medicines and allergies so every doctor sees the full picture.
Consults, medicines, lab tests, companions and SOS are a tap away for the whole family.

items.a: Most communities pay a monthly fee per home through the association; employers and senior-living homes pay per person covered, and families can subscribe directly. Consult fees, medicines and lab tests are paid when used.

items.q: Do people have to share their medical records?
items.a: No. Each person decides what doctors and hospitals can see, and can change it anytime in the app. Associations and employers never see medical details.

items.q: Which hospitals are in the network?
items.a: We partner with multispecialty hospitals near you. During the walkthrough we show you the hospitals and travel times for your location.

items.q: What if someone does not use a smartphone?
items.a: Family members can manage a parent's account, and the community desk can raise an SOS or book a service on a resident's behalf.
Usually two to four weeks from the walkthrough for a community, and a few days for a family.
No. SOS adds a faster route with your records ready. You can always call 108 as well.

cta.title: Give every home a care team on call.
cta.body: Walkthroughs are free and take about 45 minutes.
